correctness.rationale: Heuer–Striker Theorem 3.5 supplies exactly 0<=every initial row/column sum<=1; each length-k prefix normal has Frobenius norm sqrt(k). For a radius rho inball, first-row n coordinates are at least rho and sum <=1-rho sqrt(n), giving rho<=1/(n+sqrt(n)); transpose yields the m bound. Uniform entries r attain all inequalities. At optimum, the longer first row/column is fixed to r; perturbations with appropriate opposite signed small increments make every other prefix inequality strict, yielding affine dimensions mn-max(m,n) for rectangular and (n-1)^2 for square. Matching polytope has every coordinate >=rho so full row/column sum saturation forces the unique uniform center. Contact counts arise from exactly those active facets. Explicit 2-by-2 interval r(sqrt2-1)<=z<=r agrees. Full dimensionality and m=n=1 endpoints checked.
residual_risks: Finite experiments do not prove unrestricted statements; proof deductions above carry general assertion.
